blocks.text: New Westminster Lots and Land: streets and boundaries

items.t: New Westminster land is a whole-city market in BC's smallest city by area: a mainland part on the north bank of the Fraser River and Queensborough, on the eastern tip of Lulu Island, across the river and reached by the Queensborough Bridge.

The board community "New Westminster" is the city itself, with 14 sub-areas from Brunette and Sapperton in the east to Queensborough across the river; city zoning, not board lines, decides what a lot can hold.

blocks.text: New Westminster Lots and Land: the housing stock

items.t: New Westminster lots are fee-simple house lots in an almost fully built-out city; the land trade is teardown, infill and assembly lots, not greenfield subdivision.

Since June 2026 the infill frame is city-wide: zones RGO-A (up to four units) and RGO-B (up to six units) permit infill housing on single detached and duplex properties across most of the city without a site-specific rezoning.

Townhouse ground sits in the RT districts of Zoning Bylaw No. 6680 (2001): the newer RT-A and RT-B (at least 836.1 m² (9,000 sq. ft.) of site area, at least 20 m of frontage and lane access), plus the older RT-2 to RT-2C and RT-3, RT-3A and RT-3B.
Subdivision and servicing run under Bylaw 7142, 2007; parcel-level works and servicing conditions are confirmed with the City for the specific parcel.

blocks.text: New Westminster Lots and Land: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Small-scale multi-unit housing (SSMUH = small-scale multi-unit housing) needed little change here: most New Westminster residential properties already permitted a house plus a secondary suite and an accessory dwelling unit (a laneway or carriage house), so their zoning was not a provincial "restricted zone."
The exception was duplex ground: Bylaw No. 8453, 2024 rezoned the roughly 160 "restricted zone" duplex properties to a new RD-1 district that permits duplexes to add rental secondary suites.

Queensborough runs on a different clock: the Province extended Queensborough's SSMUH compliance date to May 4, 2029, so the mainland infill frame and the Queensborough frame are not the same at the same time.
A secondary suite cannot be strata-titled, sold separately or used for a short-term rental, and every property with a suite pays annual secondary suite water and sewer charges.

blocks.text: New Westminster Lots and Land: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Columbia Station is the Expo Line branch point, so a Sapperton or Braid lot and a 22nd Street lot ride different branches of the same line into downtown.

Royal Columbian Hospital at 330 E Columbia St is the only hospital in the Lower Mainland immediately adjacent to a SkyTrain station (Sapperton), which is part of why Sapperton lots carry assembly interest.

Suites are not free to carry: the City's user-fee schedule sets an annual charge for a secondary suite ($652.72 basic rate in the Engineering User Fees and Rates Bylaw schedule, as amended by Bylaw No. 8496, 2024) on top of the main dwelling's charge.

Application review currently runs under an Interim Development Review Framework, first endorsed in 2024 and updated in June 2026, while provincially driven policy changes are underway — expect review practice to keep moving.

blocks.text: New Westminster Lots and Land: development and new projects

items.t: City-wide infill rezoning: Council adopted the Official Community Plan and Zoning Bylaw amendments creating the RGO-A and RGO-B infill zones in June 2026. Status: adopted (as of November 3, 2026).

Development cost charge (DCC = development cost charge) and Amenity Cost Charge update: the City consulted developers on July 9, 2025, with draft combined DCC + ACC rates (single detached shown at $199.79 per m² of parcel area in the draft table). Status: bylaw update in progress, draft rates only (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: New Westminster Lots and Land: costs and taxes

items.t: New Westminster's total 2026 residential tax rate is 4.79312 per $1,000 of assessed value on the City's 2026 mill-rate schedule, with the municipal portion at about 3.10387 per $1,000.
The City's user-fee schedule sets an annual utility user charge of $1,305.46 (basic rate) for a single detached dwelling and $652.72 for a secondary suite.

blocks.text: New Westminster Lots and Land: getting around

items.t: The Expo Line serves New Westminster at five stations — 22nd Street, New Westminster, Columbia, Sapperton and Braid — and Columbia is where the line branches.
Queensborough lots depend on the Queensborough Bridge to the mainland city and the Pattullo Bridge corridor toward Surrey; there is no SkyTrain station in Queensborough.

blocks.text: New Westminster Lots and Land: risks and due diligence

items.t: Floodplain position is set by sub-area zone — Queensborough Zone 1, North Arm Zone 2, Quay and Downtown Zone 3, Brunette Zone 4 — and the zone decides the flood diligence for the lot; the map does not set the flood construction level for a specific building, which is a parcel-level confirmation with the City.

faq.q: Is New Westminster a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In October 2026 houses in New Westminster had a sales ratio of 10%, which the reports’ scale reads as a buyers’ market, and condos and townhomes 16%, which the reports’ scale reads as a balanced market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.
